 Heard the parties at length.
2.

This anticipatory bail application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, has been preferred by the petitioner apprehending his arrest, for offences under Sections 376, 313 and 323 IPC.
3. Learned A.P.P. representing the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail.
4. The allegation in the F.I.R. is that the informant who is a major lady, stated that she was married in the year 2005 and is having a child of 16 years.
The husband of the informant died sometime in the year 2007.
Thereafter, she came in contact with this petitioner and they established physical relationship.
It is alleged that the said relationship was established on the pretext of marriage.
Further, it is alleged that she became pregnant and her pregnancy was aborted by administering some medicine.
It is alleged that sometime in the year 2024, an application was given by the Gulshan Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand.

5.

After going through the records and hearing the parties, I find that the informant lady is major and she has herself established physical relationship with this petitioner, though on the pretext of marriage and when the relationship turned sour, the instant case has been lodged.
6.
Considering the nature of allegation and the fact that the victim-informant is major, so also the fact that the sour relationship has been converted into this case
, I am inclined to enlarge this petitioner on anticipatory bail.
7. Accordingly, this Anticipatory Bail Application stands allowed.

The petitioner, above named, is directed to surrender before the learned court below within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order and on the event of his surrender or arrest, he shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) each, with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Simdega, in connection with Simdega (Mahila) P.S. Case No.10 of 2025, subject to the condition that one of the bailers should be a close relative of the petitioner and other should be a resident of State of Jharkhand, having sufficient landed property in his name or in the name of his ancestors in which he is having share and to that effect, he has to file an affidavit before the Trial Court indicating his share in the property.
(ANANDA SEN, J.) Prashant. Cp-3 Gulshan Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand.
